caseno: Death Reference No. 42 of 2004 with Criminal Appeal Nos. 950 and 1163 of 2004.
lawyer:
ABM Waliur. Rahman Khan Deputy Attorney- General and Fura Mahmuda. Assistant Attorney- General------ For the State-Petitioner. 
Md Abul Basher. State Defence Lawyer------ For the (absconding) Condemned-Accused.	
 TH Khan with Md Shamsul Huda with Moin Uddin with MH Sarder and Nizamul Islam, Advocates------ For the Appellant in Criminal Appeal No; 950 of 2004. 
Hasen Foez Siddique with Syed Mizanur Rahman. Advocates------ For the Appellant.in Criminal Appeal No. 1163 of 2004,
parties:
State ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Kajal Ahmed Jalali (absconding) ------ Condemned-Accused
full_judgment:
110. Mr TH Khan submits that in a criminal trial, the prosecution is to prove time, place and manner of occurrence by coherent evidence. But, in this case, there is no such evidence to prove those important matters beyond reasonable doubt. The Investigating Officer did not get any witness to say that the victim was kidnapped from the road-side area near Jonaki Cinema Hall, but the place of occurrence was shown there in the sketch map without having any basis. No witness of the said place of occurrence could be found out by the Investigating Officer. It is submitted further that the last Investigating Officer, all on a sudden, had brought the sole eye-witness PW 59 Shyam Mia in to the scene for the first time long after 1 year 8 months and made out a fabricated case by using this fake witness. He submits that the evidence of PW 59, alleged eye-witness in this case, is totally unworthy of credit as he did not disclose about witnessing the occurrence for a long time to anybody and now, at first disclosed it before last 'investigating officer and Magistrate on 3-3-2003 after about 1 year 8 months. With reference to case decision reported in 6 BCR (AD) 225, the learned Advocate submits that long delay in examining material witness casts serious doubt on the prosecution case. His testimony does not also inspire confidence due to inconsistencies and improbabilities unacceptable to our common sense. The learned Advocate points out that the way investigation was conducted appears to be highly motivated and perfunctory. PW 63 Md lllias (3rd investigation officer) arrested Badal Mia and Alam Khan as those persons had conversations on 7-7-2001 and 8-7-2001 with the persons who were in possession of two sets of mobile phone snatched away from victim Shujan at the time of occurrence. But those two persons were neither made accused nor witnesses in this case to unearth the truth. If the custodians of those stolen mobiles of victim Shujan, who had talks with them, could be found out, there would have been no difficulty to find out the real assailants, who took away those phone sets after killing Shujan. Next, he submits that there might be political rivalry over getting nomination from BNP in the election in between the victim and convict Dr Roushan Alam, but that does not necessarily prove any conspiracy to kill Shujah unless existence of such conspiracy is proved by evidence. It is asserted that PW 60 Akhter Hossain, who was allegedly present in a conspiracy meeting at KDH Laboratory of Dr Roushan Alam on 30-6-2001, did not say about any conversations about conspiracy to kill Shujan. Even he did not testify presence of accused Dr Roushan Alam in the said meeting. He submits that the learned Trial Judge has found him guilty of criminal conspiracy under sections 120B of the Penal Code most arbitrarily and illegally considering 164 statement of PW 60 as a substantive piece of evidence. He assertively submits that such conviction order has no foundation in the evidence at all. It is pointed out that the prosecution has tried to show involvement of Dr Roushan Alam with the offence on the basis of chemical examination report dated 20-6-2002 (Exhibit 22), because the floor mats and dust of the seized two microbuses belonging to the accused Dr Roushan Alam contained blood particles. But the trial Court did not consider that the chemical report does not disclose about getting element of human blood in those materials. He submits that it is an absurd proposition that after lapse of 10 months 23 days from the date of occurrence, it can be possible to get any substance from the vehicles containing blood, even if those were used in the commission of murder. PW 43 Abdul Awal, who examined floor mats and containing dust substance of the vehicle did not also depose that he got any element of human blood in it. The learned Advocate further contends that some GDEs and prejudicial documents were used in the case as evidence without looking into their admissibility. It is further submitted that some important witnesses like Shajeda, wife of PW 59, Amjad Hossain Ostad, a constant companion of Shujan and some others were purposely withheld by the prosecution. So, the defence should get advantage of adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act that had they been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case. In this respect, he refers the case of Rustom & others vs State reported in 11 BLC 467. He also points out the instances of misreading and non consideration of the evidence in the judgment, particularly with reference to the testimony of PW 60 Akhter Hossain, as he never deposed mentioning the name of Dr Roushan Alam to be a person present in the alleged conspiracy meeting held on 30-6-2001. Assailing the impugned judgment, the learned Advocate asserts that none of the given facts relating to criminal conspiracy, kidnapping and murder has been proved by the prosecution witnesses, but the learned Trial Judge adopted a wrong and biased approach in ascertaining guilt of the accused Dr Roushan Alam. Therefore, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. 

 113. Mr Hasen Foez Siddique, adopting the submissions made by learned Advocate Mr TH Khan. submits further that if evidence of a solitary, eye-witness is found complete, cogent, consistent, above reproach and he is found disinterested witness having integrity, conviction may be maintainable even only on the basis of such testimony of one witness. But in the present case, PW 59 was imported by the last Investigating Officer long after I year 8 months, who is found to be a man of questionable character from his own inconsistent and improbable testimony. So, his evidence should be left totally out of consideration. He relies on the case of Sanwar Hossain vs State reported in 45 DLR 489 in this respect. Next he submits that after 4 days, PW 1 lodged first information report wherein she stated that Oil 30-6-2001, some pet terrorists of Dr Roushan Alam headed by Kajal Ahmed Jalali were in the village Rupashdi and they had to flee away on that night without being able to execute their plan of killing Shujan. So, how it was possible to hold conspiracy meeting at KDH Dhaka on 30-6-2001 at 5-00 PM as stated by some witnesses of the prosecution, he questioned. He submits that there are discrepancies in the evidence about sending message of threat on the life of Shujan prior to his (Shujan) departure for Dhaka and his actual date of journey undertaken. The Investigating Officer found that conspiracy meeting was held at 5-00 PM on 1-7-2001 at KDH Dhaka whereas PW 14 Taher said that Shujan reached Dhaka at 10-00 PM on 30-6-2001. PW 2 deposed that Shujan was engaged in election campaign and meetings at Modhyapara, Maricha Kandi on 1-7-2001, and thereafter he reached Dhaka at night on that date. So, the evidence of giving information about holding conspiracy meeting on 30-6-2001 for committing murder of Shujan on his way to Dhaka, given through PWs 60, 14 and 9 Abed Ali stands contradictory and suffers from inherent improbability. Referring to the testimony of PW 63, the learned Advocate submits that the deceased was residing with one Zakir Hossain, who had last telephonic conversation with Shujan on the very night ot occurrence at 8-00 PM i.e. just before the commission of murder. But this important witness was withheld by the prosecution. Similarly, Badal Mia and Alam Khan, who had telephonic conversations through the stolen mobile sets of Shujan after the occurrence, were not made accused or witness in this case. Wife of PW 59, namely Sajeda, was also competent witness to say whereabouts of her husband after the occurrence, but she was not examined. Neither Abdul Matin nor-Shahin, who were present at the time of recovery of Shujan's injured body, have been examined. It is pointed out that Amjad Hossain Ostad was said to be in constant company with the deceased, but he was also withheld. So it is submitted that non examination of these material witnesses casts serious doubt about the prosecution story relating to kidnapping and murder and the defence side shall get benefit of adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. In this respect, he relies on the case decision reported in 11 BLC 467. It is contended further that the victim Shujan used to reside in a room of the official building of Messrs Sakura Traders at Banani belonging to Kubaishi,a citizen of Japan, whereas PW 59 said that he used to go to Shujan's residential house at Kafrul. It shows that evidence of PW 59 is not trustworthy. 

 156. The learned Advocates for the appellants have also contended that failure of the prosecution to examine some material witnesses cast doubt on the prosecution and the accused persons are entitled to get adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. 

 157. In this respect, we have seen that large number of people of village Rupashdi were examined by the prosecution, but some material and probable witnesses of the surrounding areas where from Shujan was allegedly kidnapped and his body was recovered, were not examined. DW 1 Abdul Matin deposed that many people gathered when he found an injured man lying on the roadside drain, opposite to Bangla Academy but none of them were examined by investigating officer except CS witness No.5 Md. Shaheen, but he has not been examined at the time of trial. Cited witness PW 32 Zakir Hossain, who talked with the deceased last at about 8-00 PM on the very night of occurrence and who used to reside with the victim Shujan in a mess, was also left out. Again, cited witness Sajeda, wife of eye-witness PW 59, was an important person to testify veracity of the sole eye-witness about his long unusual stay at Dinajpur after the occurrence, but she was also withheld. Amjad Hossain Ostad was a constant companion of deceased, but he was not examined. Amongst the most important left-out persons are Badal Mia and Alam Khan, who had talks with the persons holding possession of the stolen Mobile Phones belonging to the deceased. If they were examined, it would have been possible to know identity of the real assailants. They were not brought in the picture even after arrest. Even we do not find explanation as to why they were not examined and investigation was not proceeded further in that direction. In such view of the matter, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocates for the accused persons that the accused persons are entitled to get benefit of adverse presumption under section 1 14(g) of the Evidence Act for non-examination of some material witnesses. In this respect, the case of State vs Fazal and others, reported in 39 DLR (AD) 166 and Anaddi @ Ayenuddin and others vs State reported in 6 BLC 310 may be referred to.
